messages.subject: Replacing entire entries
parts:
Hi,

I have a set of data on drinking water sources that was collected from a number of surveys. Because of this, the responses are very heterogeneous. There are 397 different responses which I have sorted into groups (well water, bottled water, surface water, rain water etc). I have a csv file that has each of the original 397 responses and the corresponding group that it belongs to. For each data point in my survey I want to replace the original response with one of my groups. My problem is that I need to match and replace the entire entry for each data point. For example, one response is "covered well" and another is "public covered well". Both of these need to be reclassified as "well or borehole." The first one works fine, but the second one becomes "public well or borehole."

I was trying to use gsub but that didn't seem to work.

gsub(reclass$oresp[i],reclass$mresp[i],x$hv201)
where reclass is from my csv file and x$hv201 is my data set


Regular expressions also seemed to come up a lot. I've never used regular expressions before but am willing to give it a try if that is the only way to do this.

Elise

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Replacing entire entries
parts:
Elise,

These should be factors, which in R are just integer vectors with some bells and whistles (levels). Rather than matching the strings (which could work), try working with the function levels():

> resp <- factor(sample(c("covered well", "public covered well", "other stuff"), 100, replace=TRUE))
> head(resp)
[1] public covered well other stuff         public covered well
[4] other stuff         public covered well covered well
Levels: covered well other stuff public covered well
> levels(resp)
[1] "covered well"        "other stuff"         "public covered well"
> levels(resp) <- c("well or borehole", "others stuff", "well or borehole")
> head(resp)
[1] well or borehole others stuff     well or borehole others stuff
[5] well or borehole well or borehole
Levels: well or borehole others stuff

The take home points are that (1) levels() returns the factor levels (2) levels() specifies levels *in order* which can be used to merge to levels with levels(resp) <- # your new levels here, with old levels merged.

HTH,
Vince
